title: Hymns to the Bodiless Hosts
subtitle: For the Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and all the Bodiless Powers, November 8
source: The apolytikion in the public-domain English of The Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom: The Greek Text with a Rendering in English (London: Williams & Norgate, 1914); the kontakion and the hymn to the Theotokos in that of Isabel Florence Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church (Boston, 1906). The closing prayer is by the editors of Purify.

sections.title: On the feast
sections.framing: The Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the other Bodiless Powers (November 8 on either calendar reckoning) is the principal feast of the angels in the Eastern Orthodox year. It is set on the eighth day of the ninth month from March (the month of the Annunciation), the eighth recalling the day of the Resurrection and the age to come, the ninth signalling the nine angelic orders Pseudo-Dionysius enumerates in The Celestial Hierarchy.
paragraphs: Hymns of the feast of the Archangel Michael and all the Bodiless Powers. The apolytikion is given in the public-domain English of a Greek and English Liturgy printed in London in 1914; the kontakion, and the first hymn to the Theotokos, in Isabel Florence Hapgood's of 1906, where the kontakion is the hymn of the Bodiless Powers sung on Mondays. The English of the megalynaria and of the second hymn to the Theotokos is ours, and so is the closing prayer.

sections.title: Apolytikion (Tone 4)
paragraphs: O Leaders of the Heavenly Hosts, unworthy as we are, we implore you that by your prayers you will encircle us with the protection of your wings of unseen glory; guard us who bend low before you and fervently cry: Release us from dangers, O Marshals of the Powers Above.
sections.citation: The Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom, Greek and English (London, 1914), pp. 116-117, the Dismissal Hymn for November 8

sections.title: Kontakion (Tone 2)
paragraphs: O ye Chieftains of God, servitors of the divine glory, Guides of men and Captains of the Bodiless Powers: Entreat that which is profitable for us, and great mercy; in that ye are the Chieftains of the Bodiless Powers.
sections.citation: Hapgood, Service Book (1906), p. 61, the hymn of the Bodiless Powers for Monday, Tone II

sections.title: Theotokion of the feast
paragraphs: More honourable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim, thou who without defilement barest God the Word, true Birth-giver of God, we magnify thee.
sections.citation: Hapgood, Service Book (1906), p. 62, the hymn to the Birth-giver of God

sections.title: Closing prayer to the Bodiless Hosts
paragraphs: O Holy Archangels and Angels of God, ye who stand before the throne of the Most High and ever look upon the face of our God in heaven: pray for us sinners that the Lord may keep us from every evil, may grant us repentance unto life, may strengthen us in the true confession of the Orthodox Faith, and at the hour of our death may send His Archangel Michael to guide our souls in peace past the spirits of the air, that with you we may glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
